_removed.ELBOW_BENT_REST: Removed 2026-08-23 - its raw signature (near-straight elbow, arm hanging back, ~164,-86,0,180) is generic enough that it was absorbing unrelated poses (confirmed: a live 'hand forward low' reading snapped to it at d=0.06). Its own servo value was already an acknowledged compromise (pan/tilt hit a mechanical hard-stop before reaching the true guard position). Don't re-add until that hard-stop is fixed (360-degree servo or reworked mount) and a real guard pose can be captured.

_disabled_positions_NOTE: Entries under _disabled_positions (below) are NOT deleted, just excluded from calibration_positions so CalibrationLoader never loads them - JSON has no real comment syntax, this is the equivalent of commenting them out. Data is fully preserved; move an entry back into calibration_positions to re-enable it.

HOOK_WINDUP.note: First point along an actual hook swing (windup -> mid -> mid -> extension), captured with capture_point.py's mean/std burst tool, real arm level/straight, no angle. A second run of this same pose came back wildly different ([163,-5,0,180]) - traced to the right arm being visible in guard during that run; CROP_RIGHT_FRAC only trims the far right edge of frame, not a raised guard near center, so that run is discarded. Recapture with the right arm fully out of frame if this one ever needs revisiting.
HOOK_WINDUP.reason_disabled: 2026-08-25 - live hook mirroring through this + HOOK_MID_1/2/EXTENSION was too unstable (see their notes - real hook elbow angles sit inside YAW_ELBOW_FADE's transition band, amplifying noise). Replaced by hook_detector.py + a scripted animation (hook_animation_test.py) for the yaw/elbow portion specifically - pan/tilt still track live. Re-enable these only if live hook interpolation is revisited.

HOOK_MID_1.note: std on yaw (19.3) and elbow (11.9) flagged high by capture_point.py. Root cause, not just 'hard to hold still': elbow's mean (155) sits inside YAW_ELBOW_FADE_START/END's transition band (170/150) in track.py, so small real elbow fluctuations during the dynamic swing flip the fade multiplier between ~0 and ~1, amplifying elbow noise into much bigger yaw noise. If mid-swing hook frames feel unstable live, this fade band overlapping real hook elbow angles is the first thing to revisit, not the capture technique.

HOOK_MID_2.note: Same fade-band variance issue as HOOK_MID_1 (yaw std 26.9, elbow std 19.5) - elbow mean 143 is also inside the 150/170 transition band. A second run of this pose ([144,-81,-98,54]) is discarded for the same right-arm-in-guard contamination reason as HOOK_WINDUP.

HOOK_EXTENSION.note: Servo elbow deliberately set to 0 (fully bent), not the 76 originally found by jogging - a real hook keeps the elbow bent through contact (compact fist, less moment of inertia - see the Hook Calibration writeup), and the first attempt at this pose drifted toward a straighter arm. The raw mediapipe reading (elbow 144, moderately open) still reflects that straighter arm from capture, so this entry intentionally pairs a 'moderately bent' raw signature with a 'fully bent' servo target. Also high variance on capture (yaw std 28.0, elbow std 24.3), same fade-band cause as the MID points. If live hook extension looks like it snaps too abruptly to fully-bent, re-capture this one for real with the elbow actually held fully bent, rather than trusting this override.

HAND_DOWN.note: Elbow raw is 115, not near the ~180 a fully-straight hanging arm should read - recorded twice (106, then 115), both far short of straight. Likely the same small-real-depth-difference weakness in MediaPipe's z as the front/behind-torso ambiguity, not a capture mistake - don't expect this to hit 180 no matter how carefully it's re-recorded.

BOXING_JAB.note: Re-recorded twice (first attempt was [150,1,-55,50] - wildly different, especially elbow 50 vs 170, confirming the pose itself is hard for MediaPipe to read stably here). Servo value not re-verified this round, carried over from before - re-check it visually if the jab still doesn't look right. User also flagged this raw reading as suspiciously close to a forward-reaching pose (HAND_FORWARD_LOW/HAND_OUT_CENTER) - may need a more deliberately distinct pose to record from.

BOXING_HOOK_SETUP.note: Elbow raw is 180 (fully straight) on both recordings, even though this pose is hand-at-ear with the elbow clearly bent - MediaPipe's elbow-plane geometry is unreliable specifically when the wrist is close to the head/shoulder in real 3D space. Treat this entry's elbow raw as low-confidence; the servo side (re-confirmed at 0,90,130,0) is the trustworthy half.
